name: r3a1-grep-denial-admitted-and-audited
description: R3a-1 Outcome 2 negative control for the canonical `knowvault_grep` workspace tool: a call by a principal without the workspace right must answer the existing content-free denial (no matches, no excerpt, no address, no workspace-id echo) and must record admission before data and its classed denial outcome through the same authorized evidence-grep boundary the production Evidence-grep read composes. internal/platform/workspaceapi/mcp_grep.go's grep tool call dispatches the authorized EvidenceGrep source and then maps its error to the content-free -32004 `workspace documents not found`. Weakening the denial guard `if err != nil` to `if err == nil` (keeping the same `writeMCPError`/`return` block verbatim so the mutated file still reads `err` and keeps its brace balance) makes a denied non-member call fall through to the success projection with an empty match page and `isError: false` instead of the existing -32004 refusal. Weakening the denial mapping from `-32004`/`workspace documents not found` to the generic `-32000`/`service unavailable` replaces the existing content-free denial with the wrong refusal. Both mutants compile and are killed behaviourally by internal/platform/workspaceapi/mcp_grep_test.go TestMCPKnowvaultGrepDenialAdmittedAndAudited, which requires the -32004 refusal with no leaked match/excerpt/address or workspace id and the `admission,denied` grep-source order.

mutations.old:
if err != nil {
		switch {
		case errors.Is(err, errMCPGrepInvalidAddress):
			writeMCPError(writer, envelope.ID, -32602, "invalid grep arguments")
			return
		case errors.Is(err, address.ErrSpanMismatch):
			writeMCPError(writer, envelope.ID, -32005, "evidence span hash mismatch")
			return
		case errors.Is(err, errMCPGrepWholeObjectUnavailable):
			writeMCPError(writer, envelope.ID, -32000, "service unavailable")
			return
		case errors.Is(err, errMCPGrepReadFragmentsInvalid):
			writeMCPError(writer, envelope.ID, -32000, "service unavailable")
			return
		}
		writeMCPError(writer, envelope.ID, -32004, "workspace documents not found")
		return
	}
mutations.new:
if err == nil {
		switch {
		case errors.Is(err, errMCPGrepInvalidAddress):
			writeMCPError(writer, envelope.ID, -32602, "invalid grep arguments")
			return
		case errors.Is(err, address.ErrSpanMismatch):
			writeMCPError(writer, envelope.ID, -32005, "evidence span hash mismatch")
			return
		case errors.Is(err, errMCPGrepWholeObjectUnavailable):
			writeMCPError(writer, envelope.ID, -32000, "service unavailable")
			return
		case errors.Is(err, errMCPGrepReadFragmentsInvalid):
			writeMCPError(writer, envelope.ID, -32000, "service unavailable")
			return
		}
		writeMCPError(writer, envelope.ID, -32004, "workspace documents not found")
		return
	}

baseline_meaning: On the unmutated tree a `knowvault_grep` call by a principal without the workspace right resolves the requested workspace through the injected EvidenceGrep source (in production the authorized grep source, which returns one content-free typed denial for a non-member, unknown or foreign workspace), so the grep tool emits the existing content-free -32004 `workspace documents not found` with no `matches` rows, no excerpt, no address and no echo of the requested workspace id. The denied membership read is journalled through the shared R1 admission-before-data mechanism with the closed denial outcome class (TestMCPKnowvaultGrepDenialAdmittedAndAudited asserts the `admission,denied:WORKSPACE_DENIED` grep-source order).
mutant_meaning: With the denial guard weakened to `if err == nil` a denied/foreign call skips the refusal and falls through to the success projection, which carries an empty match page and `isError: false`; the same weakening also refuses served calls (whose error is nil) with -32004, so the unmutated green case turns red too. With the denial mapping weakened to -32000 the same denial is answered with the generic service-unavailable refusal instead of the existing content-free -32004. Both mutated files still read `err` and keep the -32004 branch referenced, so internal/platform/workspaceapi compiles and the failure is the behavioural TestMCPKnowvaultGrepDenialAdmittedAndAudited assertion (a denied `knowvault_grep` call must return the existing denial and no content), not a build failure; each mutant is killed by the registered probe and not vacuous.
runner: tests/contracts/mutation-runner/main.go executes these cases from tests/contracts/mutation-registry.json under the GO_UNIT harness for the invariant entry `acceptance.r3a1.grep.denial-admitted-and-audited`; the identical cases are committed both here and in the registry so the proof is pinned to the product guard.
